nodes.label: V1 Scope (multi-tenant COD CRM + client portal)
Roles Are Contextual, Not a Column
Two Data Layers (Private vs Global)
nodes.rationale: Private tenant data isolated by RLS; global layer holds only hashed numbers and aggregated behavioural events.

nodes.label: Every Outcome Carries Provenance
nodes.rationale: Carrier-API-confirmed outcomes are worth far more than manual checkboxes; manual businesses are first-class but count less.

nodes.label: Confirmation Link Instead of Order Falsification
Fault Split on Every Return
nodes.rationale: Business/carrier-caused returns never count against customer; otherwise the score is unfair and untrusted.

nodes.label: Integrations Behind One Adapter Interface with Event Inbox
The Score Informs, Never Decides
nodes.rationale: No order is auto-cancelled by a score; risk policy only recommends actions.

nodes.label: Operating Modes (Manual / Assisted / Integrated)
nodes.rationale: Modes are not code paths; they describe which adapters are connected and only affect data quality / scoring confidence.

nodes.label: Permission Presets (Manager, Call agent, Logistics, Viewer)
PostgreSQL Row-Level Security per Tenant
nodes.rationale: Single most valuable safeguard: app bugs cannot leak across tenants.

nodes.label: Schema Conventions (uuid v7, numeric DZD, text enums, soft delete)
Group A: Identity, Tenancy and Access
Group D: Catalog, Orders, Delivery and Returns
Group F: Client Portal and Public Presence
Phone Ownership Proof (OTP or Confirmation Link)
nodes.rationale: Email/Google login proves nothing about a phone; score is keyed on phone numbers.

nodes.label: Phone Normalisation to E.164 + HMAC Hash
Convert Opportunity to Order
nodes.rationale: Moving to won does not auto-create an order, to avoid phantom orders.

nodes.label: Score Computation (smoothed rate, weights, modifier, tiers)
Legal Gate for Global Score
nodes.rationale: Highest-risk part of product; cross-business sharing requires lawyer opinion, ANPDP declaration, consent, k-anonymity.
